title: RFID Wet Inlay (UHF) — PSA + Glassine Liner Roll for Mark Andy, Nilpeter, MPS + Mühlbauer TAL Converters
summary: RFID wet inlays are pressure-sensitive chip-on-antenna components on 23-50 µm PET film with permanent acrylic PSA + 61 gsm yellow glassine (or PET) release liner — supplied on 76 mm (3″) cores at 2,000-10,000 inlays per roll, with web widths and pitch matched to Mark Andy P5/P7, Nilpeter FA-17, MPS EF-Symjet, Edale FL3, Mühlbauer TAL-M, Melzer ST and Bielomatik PiP converting cassettes. Default UHF chip set (Impinj M730 / M750 / M770, NXP UCODE 8 / 9, Monza R6 / R6-P, Alien Higgs-9) plus HF / NFC variants (NTAG21x, NTAG 424 DNA, MIFARE Ultralight, ICODE SLIX2). 100% RF-tested at converting speed; per-lot sensitivity histogram + yield report + GS1 SGTIN-96 EPC manifest in CSV/XML. Auburn ARC + Walmart T2/T3 + Target SUPPLIERS + Macy's audit-ready.
heroPoints: PSA + glassine release liner — peel-and-stick onto thermal-transfer / direct-thermal / synthetic label face stock at converter; 50-150 m/min line speed.
Roll format 2,000-10,000 inlays / 3″ core; web widths 45 / 50 / 58 / 76 / 100 mm; pitch 14 / 16 / 18 / 20 / 22 / 25 / 30 / 35 mm matched to converter cassette geometry.
Adhesive grade options — general-purpose acrylic (FTM 2 ≥18 N/25 mm), all-temperature cryo-grade (-40 °C), low-surface-energy rubber-based, removable low-tack — specified per FINAT FTM.
imageAlt: RFID wet inlay roll on 3-inch core — Impinj M730 chip on aluminium-etched antenna with permanent acrylic PSA + 61 gsm yellow glassine release liner, ready for label converter at 22 mm pitch on 76 mm web

brief.label: What wet inlay is + what it is not
items: Wet inlay = chip + antenna on PET film + permanent acrylic PSA + silicone-coated PET / glassine release liner.
Designed for label converters laminating between thermal-transfer / direct-thermal / synthetic / paper face stock and primary liner.
Sister: rfid-dry-inlay = same chip + antenna WITHOUT adhesive or liner — for ID-1 card press, hard-tag housing, over-mold.
Choose wet for label-stock lamination + roll-to-roll converter. Choose dry for ISO 7810 PVC card press + injection over-mold.

brief.label: Substrate, antenna and chip-attach
items: Face film — 23 µm or 50 µm PET; aluminium-etched antenna (cost-optimised) or copper-etched (premium).
Chip-attach — anisotropic conductive paste (ACP) for PET; thermocompression / wire-bond for polyimide / PEN (high-temp variant).
Cpk > 1.33 on read-range and chip sensitivity per 100% RF-tested production line.
Antenna geometry library — dogbone 96 mm, rectangular 70 mm, short dipole 50 mm, near-field 27 mm, square 50 mm, web 44 mm.

brief.label: Adhesive grades — match to face stock + end-use
items: General-purpose permanent acrylic — paper / cardboard / synthetic at room temperature; FTM 2 peel ≥18 N/25 mm.
All-temperature cryo-grade acrylic — -40 °C cold-chain / freezer; cross-linked promoter, 200-cycle freeze-thaw stable per ASTM D3330.
Low-surface-energy rubber / modified acrylic — polyethylene / polypropylene / PE-coated paper; tackifier-loaded for LSE wet-out.
Removable low-tack acrylic — returnable-asset / event-wristband / temporary-promotion; FTM 2 peel 50-150 g/25 mm.
High-tack acrylic — corrugated case / kraft / textile; FTM 2 peel ≥25 N/25 mm.
All graded per FINAT FTM 1 (peel adhesion), FTM 2 (180° peel), FTM 8 (shear), FTM 9 (loop tack), FTM 19 (release force).

brief.label: Release liner options
items: Standard 61 gsm yellow glassine — paper liner; room-temperature web converting at <50 m/min.
PET release liner 50-75 µm — for high-speed (>50 m/min) or low-tack inlays where glassine tears.
Clear PET liner — for see-through label converting and inspection-window applications.
Silicone release force 10-25 g/25 mm at FINAT FTM 19 — specified on per-lot COA.
Liner side identification — yellow glassine has visible facing; PET liner often clear or tinted.

brief.label: Roll format — web width + pitch + core
items: Core — 76.2 mm (3″) standard; 152 mm (6″) for high-speed converting lines.
Roll outer diameter — 300 mm OD ≈ 5,000-8,000 inlays; 400 mm OD ≈ 10,000-16,000 inlays.
Web widths — 45 / 50 / 58 / 76 / 100 mm; specifying width wrong forces a slitting pass and adds 0.3-0.8 ¢/inlay.
Pitch — 14 / 16 / 18 / 20 / 22 / 25 / 30 / 35 mm or custom; pitch tolerance ±0.5 mm + chip position ±0.3 mm.
Splice — ≤1 splice / 2,000 inlays, marked with 25 mm metallic tag for line auto-detection.

Card press equipment — Mühlbauer CL, Melzer CLX, HID FARGO, Matica MX, Atlantic Zeiser DigiLine.

For label converter laminating into thermal-transfer / direct-thermal / synthetic label stock.

sections.title: FINAT FTM + Auburn ARC — the QC framework converters specify in the RFP

dataHighlight.heading: FTM 1 peel adhesion + FTM 2 180° peel + FTM 8 shear + FTM 9 loop tack + FTM 19 release force — the 5 measurements that gate every wet inlay roll
dataHighlight.text: FINAT (Féderation INternationale des fabricants et transformateurs d'Adhésifs et Thermocollants sur papiers et autres supports) Technical Method (FTM) tests are the labelstock industry's standard QC framework, applied to every wet inlay roll. FTM 1 measures peel adhesion against stainless steel; FTM 2 measures 180° peel against the target face stock; FTM 8 measures shear holding power (resistance to slip under sustained load); FTM 9 measures loop tack (initial bond strength on first contact); FTM 19 measures the release-liner force (10-25 g/25 mm typical) that the converter unwinder needs. For UHF retail programmes, Auburn University RFID Lab ARC categories add a parallel certification — Q (high-volume retail), W (apparel), G (general purpose), X (cold-DC), L (logistics), M (RTI / metal-near) — based on 60 cm + 6 m anechoic chamber tests with population sweep. Walmart Tier 2 + Tier 3, Target SUPPLIERS portal, Macy's, Nordstrom, Dick's, Lululemon and Decathlon all reference Auburn ARC categories in their vendor-compliance specifications. Per-lot quality pack ships with every order ≥50,000 inlays — sensitivity histogram (dBm distribution across the 100%-tested roll), yield report (rejects-removed count + roll-position), GS1 SGTIN-96 / SSCC-96 / GIAI-96 / GRAI-96 EPC manifest in CSV or XML keyed to roll position, and FINAT FTM measurements per the customer's adhesive-grade RFP.
dataHighlight.source: FINAT, Technical Handbook + FTM 1-19 Test Methods (finat.com, 2023); Auburn University RFID Lab, ARC Category Specifications (rfid.auburn.edu, 2024); GS1, EPC Tag Data Standard 2.0 (ref.gs1.org, 2022)

bullets: FTM 2 180° peel must match the face stock — paper / synthetic / fabric / corrugated have very different bond requirements.
FTM 19 release force determines whether the liner tears at converter speed — PET liner is the fix for >50 m/min lines.
Auburn ARC category drives the chip + antenna combo — ARC-W for apparel hang-tag, ARC-X for cold-DC pallet.

faq.question: What is the difference between a wet inlay and a dry inlay?
faq.answer: A wet inlay includes a permanent acrylic pressure-sensitive adhesive backing with a 61 gsm yellow glassine (or PET) release liner — ready to peel-and-stick to a face-stock surface or laminate into a label structure on a Mark Andy P5/P7, Nilpeter FA-17, MPS EF-Symjet, Edale FL3, Bobst M5/M6 or OMET Varyflex converter at 50-150 m/min. A dry inlay has no adhesive and no liner — it is a bare 23-50 µm PET (or polyimide / PEN for high-temp) film with chip and antenna, designed to be laminated between card / tag / housing layers using heat + pressure, ultrasonic bond, or 200-280 °C injection over-mold. Wet inlays are used by label converters; dry inlays are used by card manufacturers (ISO 7810 PVC / PC press), hard-tag assemblers and over-mold tag producers.

faq.question: What quality testing is performed on wet inlays before shipment?
faq.answer: Every wet inlay undergoes 100% inline RF testing during production at converting speed — each inlay is individually read-tested by a high-speed RFID reader on the production line. Any inlay that fails to respond or falls below the minimum sensitivity threshold is marked with a reject flag and excluded from the roll, with the roll-position logged for the per-lot yield report. We also perform statistical sampling for read-range measurement, FINAT FTM 1 / 2 / 8 / 9 / 19 adhesive-peel-tack-shear-release tests per the customer's adhesive-grade RFP, and Auburn ARC environmental stress testing for retail / cold-DC / industrial use cases. Per-lot quality pack — sensitivity histogram + yield report + GS1 EPC manifest + FINAT FTM measurements + COA — ships with every order ≥50,000 inlays.

faq.question: Can wet inlays be pre-encoded with custom data before shipment?
faq.answer: Yes. We offer pre-encoding services including GS1 SGTIN-96 / SGTIN-198 / SSCC-96 / GIAI-96 / GRAI-96 EPC writing (sequential, random, or customer-supplied list with TID-based serialisation), NFC NDEF URL / vCard / Smart Poster programming, lock bit + access-password arming per programme spec, and full per-roll EPC manifest in CSV or XML keyed to roll position so downstream label printers correlate printed GTIN + serial to the encoded EPC for traceability. Pre-encoding adds minimal lead time (1-3 days) and is recommended for large production runs where on-site encoding would bottleneck converter line speed. Encoding data is provided via CSV upload or REST API integration to our pre-encoding service.

faq.question: Which chip should I specify when I don't know what my end customer needs yet?
faq.answer: For NFC converting lines that need one flexible stocking inlay, NTAG213 is the mainstream choice — {chip:nxp-ntag-213:user_bytes} bytes user memory, standard NDEF URL fit, widest smartphone compatibility, lowest per-unit cost. For UHF, {chip:impinj-m730:name} is the equivalent default — 96-bit EPC, no user memory to complicate encoding, volume pricing, Auburn ARC-W certified at standard antenna sizes. Stock these two chips as your base inventory and layer in speciality variants (NTAG 424 DNA for cryptographic authentication, NTAG215 for Amiibo-compatible long-URL, M770 for mixed-surface cold-DC, UCODE 9 for dense-reader 18 m range) as customer requirements firm up. Avoid stocking NFC and UHF on the same web width or you'll waste feeder changeover time — keep the two frequency families on dedicated converter cassettes.

faq.question: How do I match wet-inlay adhesive to the end-use substrate?
faq.answer: For standard paper and cardboard face stocks at room temperature, a general-purpose permanent acrylic (180-day peel adhesion per FINAT FTM 2, peel ≥18 N/25 mm) is the correct default. For low-surface-energy substrates (polyethylene, polypropylene, PE-coated paper), specify a rubber-based or modified acrylic with tackifier loading to wet out the plastic. For cold-chain and frozen applications (pharma cold-storage, frozen food), an all-temperature cryo-grade acrylic rated to -40 °C is mandatory — standard acrylic loses bond at <-5 °C. For removable labels (returnable asset tags, event wristbands, temporary promotion), specify a low-tack acrylic with FTM 2 peel of 50-150 g/25 mm. For corrugated case + kraft + textile, specify a high-tack acrylic with FTM 2 peel ≥25 N/25 mm. Always run FINAT FTM 1 / FTM 2 / FTM 9 (peel + tack) tests on the target face stock before committing to a production run — and we supply 100-piece sample rolls at no charge for converter qualification.
